units.translation: of the dead to whom sacrifices are offered. Schol. ἄτιμος ἐμπύροισι [dishonored among the burnt offerings] (codex ἐν πυροῖσι [in the wheat]) κνισωτοῖς ἔσῃ παρ᾿ εὐδείπνοις χθονός [you will be with the savory feasts of the earth], that is, honored with a feast among the departed. Thus the sequence: while the other dead receive offerings, you will be dishonored. Etym. Μ αἰώρα [the Swing festival]: a festival of Athena, which they call εὔδειπνον [the good feast]; for it is said that Erigone, daughter of Aegisthus and Clytemnestra, came to Athens with her grandfather Tyndareus. Similarly Hesychius s.v. εὐδείπνοις [to the good feasts]. Photius p. 28, 14 εὐδείπνους [the good feasts]: the libations brought to the dead. εὔδειπνοι δαῖτες [good feasts] is in Eurip. Med. 200. From these it can be gathered that εὐδείπνοις [good feasts] in Aeschylus is used adjectivally, ἐμπύροισι [burnt offerings] substantivally.
For thus would lawful feasts of mortals be established for you; but if not, you will be dishonored among the savory burnt offerings of the earth.
